blocks.text: Practice long questions for the whole of Unit 11 (Trigonometric Functions and their Graphs), in the shape of a Board Section-II question part: each carries 5 marks (a longer problem, a proof or a derivation). Each one is solved in full, step by step.

blocks.prompt: 1 Using the unit circle, find the domain and the range of \(\sin\theta\) and \(\cos\theta\). Hence explain why \(2\cos\theta = 3\) has no solution. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Read \(\cos\theta\) and \(\sin\theta\) as the coordinates of the terminal point, then use \(x^{2} + y^{2} = 1\).

book_ref.quote: Every point of the unit circle satisfies

steps: Let the terminal side of \(\theta\) meet the unit circle at \(P(x, y)\); then \(\cos\theta = x\) and \(\sin\theta = y\)
For every real \(\theta\) there is exactly one such point, so each of \(\cos\theta\), \(\sin\theta\) has one value: domain \(= \mathbb{R}\) for both
On the unit circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = 1\); since \(y^{2} \ge 0\), \(x^{2} \le 1\), so \(-1 \le x \le 1\); similarly \(-1 \le y \le 1\)
The values \(\pm 1\) are reached at the axis points, e.g. \(\cos 0 = 1\), \(\cos\pi = -1\), \(\sin\frac{\pi}{2} = 1\), \(\sin\frac{3\pi}{2} = -1\): range \(= [-1, 1]\) for both
\(2\cos\theta = 3\) needs \(\cos\theta = \frac{3}{2} = 1.5 > 1\), outside \([-1, 1]\); so there is no solution
blocks.final_answer: Domain of \(\sin\theta\) and \(\cos\theta\): \(\mathbb{R}\); range: \([-1, 1]\); \(2\cos\theta = 3\) is impossible

blocks.prompt: 2 Find the domain and the range of \(\tan\theta\) and of \(\cot\theta\), giving reasons. List the excluded angles in \([-2\pi, 2\pi]\) for each. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Write each as a fraction of the coordinates of \(P(x, y)\) and remove the angles where the denominator is zero.

book_ref.quote: therefore the range of tangent function

steps: \(\tan\theta = \frac{y}{x}\) needs \(x \ne 0\): the terminal side must not lie on the \(Y\)-axis, i.e. \(\theta \ne (2n + 1)\frac{\pi}{2}\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\)
In \([-2\pi, 2\pi]\) the excluded angles for \(\tan\theta\) are \(\pm\frac{\pi}{2}, \pm\frac{3\pi}{2}\); domain \(= \mathbb{R} - \{(2n + 1)\frac{\pi}{2}\}\)
Near \(B(0, 1)\), \(y \to 1\) and \(x \to 0\), so \(\frac{y}{x} \to \pm\infty\); \(\tan\theta\) takes every real value: range \(= \mathbb{R}\)
\(\cot\theta = \frac{x}{y}\) needs \(y \ne 0\): not on the \(X\)-axis, \(\theta \ne n\pi\); in \([-2\pi, 2\pi]\): \(-2\pi, -\pi, 0, \pi, 2\pi\) excluded

blocks.prompt: 3 Find the domain and the range of \(\sec\theta\). Hence decide whether \(\sec\theta = -\frac{1}{2}\) and \(\sec\theta = -\frac{5}{2}\) are possible. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Use \(\sec\theta = \frac{1}{x}\) with \(x = \cos\theta\), remove \(x = 0\), and take reciprocals of \(0 < x \le 1\) and \(-1 \le x < 0\).

book_ref.quote: Dividing \(1\) by a positive number that is at most

steps: \(\sec\theta\) takes all values except those strictly between \(-1\) and \(1\): range \(= \mathbb{R} - (-1, 1) = (-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)

blocks.prompt: 4 Find the domain and the range of \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta\). Hence find the values of \(k\) for which \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta = k\) has a solution, and test \(k = 0.8\) and \(k = 4\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Use \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta = \frac{1}{y}\) with \(y = \sin\theta\), remove \(y = 0\), and take reciprocals.

book_ref.quote: attains all values except those between

steps: \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta = \frac{1}{y}\), \(y = \sin\theta\); it needs \(y \ne 0\): the terminal side not on the \(X\)-axis, \(\theta \ne n\pi\)
Domain \(= \mathbb{R} - \{n\pi : n \in \mathbb{Z}\}\), the same as that of \(\cot\theta\)
Range \(= \mathbb{R} - \{x \mid -1 < x < 1\} = (-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\); so a solution exists exactly when \(|k| \ge 1\)
\(k = 0.8\): \(|k| < 1\), no solution. \(k = 4\): \(\sin\theta = \frac{1}{4}\), which is in \([-1, 1]\), so a solution exists
blocks.final_answer: Domain \(\mathbb{R} - \{n\pi\}\), range \((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\); solvable iff \(|k| \ge 1\): \(0.8\) no, \(4\) yes

blocks.prompt: 5 Determine whether each function is even, odd or neither: (i) \(f(x) = x^{2}\sin x\) (ii) \(g(x) = \dfrac{\cos x}{1 + x^{2}}\) (iii) \(h(x) = x + \cos x\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Replace \(x\) by \(-x\), use \(\sin(-x) = -\sin x\) and \(\cos(-x) = \cos x\), and compare with the original.

book_ref.quote: The graph of an odd function is always symmetric about the origin.

steps: So \(h\) is neither even nor odd; one value is enough to show this

blocks.prompt: 6 Using \(\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta\) and \(\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta\), show that \(\tan\theta\), \(\cot\theta\) and \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta\) are odd and \(\sec\theta\) is even. Hence decide whether \(\sec x\tan x\) is even or odd. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Write each function through sine and cosine and replace \(\theta\) by \(-\theta\).

book_ref.quote: The graph of an even function is always symmetric about the

steps: For \(F(x) = \sec x\tan x\): \(F(-x) = \sec(-x)\tan(-x) = \sec x(-\tan x) = -F(x)\): odd
blocks.final_answer: \(\tan\), \(\cot\), \(\operatorname{cosec}\) odd; \(\sec\) even; \(\sec x\tan x\) is odd

blocks.prompt: 7 By the method used for the period of sine, prove that the period of \(\cos\theta\) is \(2\pi\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Let \(p\) be the period, put a convenient \(\theta\) to get a list of candidates, then test the smallest positive one.

book_ref.quote: Theorem 11.1: Sine is a periodic function

steps: Suppose \(p > 0\) is the period: \(\cos(\theta + p) = \cos\theta\) for all \(\theta \in \mathbb{R}\) ... (C)
Put \(\theta = 0\): \(\cos p = \cos 0 = 1\), so \(p\) is one of \(2\pi, 4\pi, 6\pi, \ldots\) (\(p = 0\) is not positive)
No positive number smaller than \(2\pi\) has \(\cos p = 1\); e.g. \(p = \pi\) gives \(\cos\pi = -1 \ne 1\), so \(\pi\) fails
\(p = 2\pi\): adding \(2\pi\) is one full turn, which brings the terminal point back to itself, so \(\cos(\theta + 2\pi) = \cos\theta\) for every \(\theta\)
\(2\pi\) is the smallest positive number satisfying (C), so the period of \(\cos\theta\) is \(2\pi\)

blocks.prompt: 8 By the method used for the period of tangent, prove that the period of \(\cot\theta\) is \(\pi\). Hence find the period of \(\cot 3\theta\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Put \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}\) (where \(\cot\theta = 0\)) to get the candidates; then show that \(\pi\) works for every \(\theta\).

book_ref.quote: Theorem 11.2: Tangent is a periodic function

steps: Suppose \(p > 0\) is the period: \(\cot(\theta + p) = \cot\theta\) for all \(\theta\) in the domain ... (D)
Put \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}\): \(\cot\left(\frac{\pi}{2} + p\right) = \cot\frac{\pi}{2} = 0\), so \(\frac{\pi}{2} + p\) is an odd multiple of \(\frac{\pi}{2}\): \(p = \pi, 2\pi, 3\pi, \ldots\)
\(\pi\) is the smallest candidate, so the period of \(\cot\theta\) is \(\pi\)
blocks.final_answer: Period of \(\cot\theta\) is \(\pi\); period of \(\cot 3\theta\) is \(\frac{\pi}{3}\)

blocks.prompt: 9 Find the periods of (i) \(\cos 4x\) (ii) \(1 - 3\tan\frac{2x}{5}\), showing the working. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Add the known period of the basic function to the angle and rewrite it as the coefficient times \(x\) plus a shift.

book_ref.quote: Two conditions are packed into this definition

steps: \(\tan\left(\frac{2x}{5} + \pi\right) = \tan\frac{2}{5}\left(x + \frac{5\pi}{2}\right)\), so the value repeats when \(x\) increases by \(\frac{5\pi}{2}\)
The constant 1 and the factor \(-3\) do not change the period: the period of \(1 - 3\tan\frac{2x}{5}\) is \(\frac{5\pi}{2}\)

blocks.prompt: 10 Without a calculator, evaluate \(\sin 120^{\circ}\cos 330^{\circ} + \cos 240^{\circ}\sin(-30^{\circ})\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Reduce each angle to a basic angle with the identities for \(-\theta\), \(180^{\circ} \pm \theta\) and \(360^{\circ} - \theta\).

book_ref.quote: The method is always the same three steps

blocks.prompt: 11 Find the values of all six trigonometric functions of \(225^{\circ}\), and check their signs with the quadrant. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Write \(225^{\circ} = 180^{\circ} + 45^{\circ}\) and use the identities for \(\pi + \theta\).

book_ref.quote: Check every answer with the quadrant

steps: \(225^{\circ} = 180^{\circ} + 45^{\circ}\) lies in Quadrant III, where only tangent (and cotangent) are positive
Signs check: sine, cosine and their reciprocals negative, tangent and cotangent positive, as Quadrant III requires

blocks.prompt: 12 Make a table of values and draw the graph of \(y = 2\sin x\) for \(0 \le x \le 2\pi\). State its maximum and minimum values and where they occur. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Double each value of \(\sin x\) at the marks \(0, \frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{\pi}{2}, \ldots, 2\pi\), plot the points and join them smoothly.

book_ref.quote: The table of the ordered pairs satisfying \(y = \sin x\) is as follows:

steps: Take \(x\) along the \(X\)-axis and \(y\) along the \(Y\)-axis, plot the nine points and join them with one smooth curve
The curve lies between \(y = 2\) and \(y = -2\), since \(-1 \le \sin x \le 1\) gives \(-2 \le 2\sin x \le 2\); it cuts the \(x\)-axis at \(0, \pi, 2\pi\)
Maximum \(2\) at \(x = \frac{\pi}{2}\); minimum \(-2\) at \(x = \frac{3\pi}{2}\); same period \(2\pi\) as \(\sin x\)

blocks.prompt: 13 Make a table of values and draw the graph of \(y = 1 + \cos x\) for \(0 \le x \le 2\pi\). State its range and where it touches the \(x\)-axis. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Add 1 to each value of \(\cos x\) at the main marks, plot and join smoothly.

book_ref.quote: The table of the ordered pairs satisfying \(y = \cos x\) is as follows:

steps: Plot the points and join them with a smooth curve: it is the cosine curve moved 1 unit up
Since \(-1 \le \cos x \le 1\), \(0 \le 1 + \cos x \le 2\): range \([0, 2]\); maximum 2 at \(x = 0, 2\pi\)
It touches the \(x\)-axis only where \(\cos x = -1\), i.e. at \(x = \pi\)

blocks.prompt: 14 Draw the graph of \(y = \tan x\) for \(-\frac{\pi}{2} < x < \frac{\pi}{2}\) using the points \(0, \pm\frac{\pi}{6}, \pm\frac{\pi}{4}, \pm\frac{\pi}{3}\). Describe its behaviour near the ends. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Use \(\tan(-x) = -\tan x\) for the negative angles, draw the asymptotes, then join the points with a rising curve.

book_ref.quote: so we shall first draw the graph for the interval from

steps: Draw dashed vertical asymptotes \(x = -\frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(x = \frac{\pi}{2}\), where \(\cos x = 0\) and \(\tan x\) is undefined
Plot the seven points and join them with one smooth curve rising from left to right, through the origin
As \(x \to \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)^{-}\), \(\tan x \to +\infty\); as \(x \to \left(-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)^{+}\), \(\tan x \to -\infty\); the curve never meets the asymptotes
blocks.final_answer: Increasing curve through \((0, 0)\) with asymptotes \(x = \pm\frac{\pi}{2}\); range \(\mathbb{R}\)

blocks.prompt: 15 Find the maximum and minimum values of \(f(x) = 3 - 2\sin\left(2x + \frac{\pi}{4}\right)\) and of its reciprocal \(\dfrac{1}{f(x)}\). Give one value of \(x\) where \(f\) is largest. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Use \(M = a + |b|\), \(m = a - |b|\); with \(b < 0\) the maximum is where the sine is \(-1\); for a positive function the reciprocal swaps maximum and minimum.

book_ref.quote: Now consider the general form of a sinusoidal function

steps: For a positive function the largest value of \(\frac{1}{f}\) comes from the smallest value of \(f\): maximum of \(\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{1} = 1\)

blocks.prompt: 16 For \(y = -1 + 3\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}x - \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) find the vertical shift, the amplitude, the period, the maximum and minimum values, and the first positive \(x\) where each occurs. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Compare with \(a + b\cos(cx + d)\); period \(= \frac{2\pi}{c}\), \(M = a + |b|\), \(m = a - |b|\).

book_ref.quote: the maximum height of the wave measured from its midline

blocks.prompt: 17 A Ferris wheel of radius 25 m has its lowest point 3 m above the ground and makes one revolution every 40 seconds. A rider gets on at the lowest point. Model the height h(t) of the rider, find the height after 25 seconds, and find when the rider first reaches the top. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Period gives \(c\), the radius gives \(b\), the height of the centre gives \(a\); a start at the bottom needs \(a - b\cos(ct)\).

book_ref.quote: Choosing the starting function: start at the top

blocks.prompt: 18 The depth of water at a harbour is \(D(t) = 7 + 3\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}t\right)\) metres, \(t\) in hours after midnight. Find (a) the depth at \(t = 4\) (b) the greatest and least depths and when they first occur (c) the time for one full cycle. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Substitute for (a); use \(M = a + |b|\), \(m = a - |b|\) with \(\cos = \pm 1\) for (b); period \(= \frac{2\pi}{c}\) for (c).

book_ref.quote: The first Ferris wheel was invented by George W. Ferris

steps: (b) \(a = 7\), \(b = 3\): greatest depth \(7 + 3 = 10\) m when \(\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}t\right) = 1\), i.e. at \(t = 0\) (midnight), again at \(t = 12\)
Check: \(5.5\) lies between 4 and 10, and \(t = 4\) is on the way down from the high level at \(t = 0\) to the low level at \(t = 6\)
blocks.final_answer: (a) \(5.5\) m (b) greatest \(10\) m at \(t = 0\); least \(4\) m at \(t = 6\) (c) \(12\) hours

blocks.prompt: 19 At a beach the water level is highest, 14 ft, at t = 0 hours and lowest, 4 ft, at t = 6 hours, and it varies sinusoidally. Model the level L(t) and find the level at t = 2 hours and the first time after t = 6 at which it is highest again. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Amplitude \(= \frac{M - m}{2}\), midline \(= \frac{M + m}{2}\); high to low is half a period; a start at the top needs \(a + b\cos(ct)\).

book_ref.quote: Every problem follows the same plan

steps: High to low takes half a period: period \(= 2 \times 6 = 12\) hours, so \(c = \dfrac{2\pi}{12} = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\)
Highest again one period after \(t = 0\): \(t = 12\) hours

blocks.prompt: 20 From a point 50 m above the surface of a lake, the angle of elevation of the top of a tower is \(30^{\circ}\) and the angle of depression of its image in the lake is \(45^{\circ}\). Find the height of the tower above the lake. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Let the height be \(h\) and the horizontal distance \(y\); the image is \(h\) below the surface, so write two tangent equations and remove \(y\).

book_ref.quote: the image in the water is as far below the surface as the peak is above it

steps: The top is \(h - 50\) above the observer's level; the image is \(50 + h\) below it
